title: NKT cells and CD8+ T cells are dispensable for T cell dependent allergic airway inflammation
protocol: Induction of AAI should be carried out as described elsewhere.
Sensitise six to eight-week-old male mice with intraperitoneal injections of OVA plus 1 mg aluminum hydroxide in 0.2 ml PBS on days 0 and 7.
Give mice 50 μl of 2 mg/ml OVA in sterile PBS via the intranasal route on days 14-17.
Harvest bilateral BAL with 2 aliquots of 1 ml PBS containing 0.6 mM EDTA, 24 hours after the last intranasal challenge.
Collect tissues for histological analysis.
Mice can be challenged via the intranasal route on days 19, 21, 24 and 26 using a second protocol.
Euthanize animals 24 hours after the last challenge.
Collect BAL fluid to determine cellular infiltration and cytokine levels.
Harvest perfused lungs for histological studies.
For depletion of CD8+ T cells or NKT cells from specified mouse strains, inject 100 μg/mouse/week of specific antibody for 4 weeks.
Confirm effectiveness by staining splenocytes with CD1d:Ig dimer and CD8-specific antibody.
Measure inflammatory mediators in cell-free BAL fluid by ELISA for IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13.
Resuspend cells in HBSS and enumerate using a hemocytometer.
Concentrate cells onto microscope slides by cytocentrifugation.
Stain cells with Wright–Giemsa stain to determine leukocyte differentials after counting 200 cells.
Euthanize mice by CO₂ inhalation.
Remove lungs and embed in paraffin.
Cut sections into 5 to 6 μm using a cryostat.
Stain the sections with hematoxylin/eosin (H&E) for examination under a microscope.
Perform mucus staining with PAS.
Score disease severity based on cellular infiltration observed microscopically.
Stain paraffin sections with Alcian blue/periodic acid-Schiff stain to observe mucus-producing cells.
